#### Titus (D) c. 80--90 CE

The Letter of Paul to Titus

**NAME, AUTHORSHIP, AND BACKGROUND**

This letter, which has many similarities to 1 Timothy, is named for its recipient, Paul\'s envoy and co-worker Titus. It is cast as a reminder and incitement to Titus to complete his mission on Crete ([1.5](javascript:void(0))). Acts and the other Pauline letters do not mention any apostolic mission on this, the largest of the Aegean islands and home to a large Jewish community. Those who argue that the letter is genuine contend that such a mission could have taken place after Paul\'s imprisonment at Rome recounted in [Acts 28](javascript:void(0)), while those who regard it as pseudepigraphical (see [Introduction to the Pastoral Epistles](javascript:void(0)), [1725](javascript:void(0))) think the author has chosen Crete as a locale representing quintessential disobedience ([1.12](javascript:void(0))), or because of a later tradition associating Titus with the island.

Although Titus is not mentioned in Acts, Paul\'s letters ascribe a prominent role to an associate named Titus. According to [Gal 2.3](javascript:void(0)) Titus was a Gentile who accompanied Paul to the conference with the Jerusalem apostles, where Titus served as a litmus test for the acceptability of uncircumcised Gentile converts. Titus played a crucial role in the pastoral ministry to Corinth, first as a key administrator of the collection for the church in Jerusalem ([2 Cor 8.6](javascript:void(0)),[16](javascript:void(0))--[17](javascript:void(0)),[23](javascript:void(0)); [12.18](clbr://internal.sandbox/book/OEBPS/012_part1zzb.xhtml#twocor12_18)), and later as Paul\'s diplomatic envoy who successfully brokered a reconciliation between the apostle and the Corinthian church, which had harbored doubts about Paul\'s legitimacy and financial reliability ([2 Cor 2.13](clbr://internal.sandbox/book/OEBPS/012_part1zzb.xhtml#twocor2_13); [7.6](javascript:void(0))--[7](javascript:void(0)),[13](javascript:void(0))--[16](javascript:void(0))).

**STRUCTURE AND INTERPRETATION**

The letter to Titus is framed as a commissioning letter. After the usual epistolary prescript ([1.1](javascript:void(0))--[4](javascript:void(0)), which is expanded with a theological creed), the body of the letter focuses on Titus\'s dual mandate to correct things on Crete and to appoint elders ([1.5](javascript:void(0))--[16](javascript:void(0))). The basis for his ministry follows in instructions concerning the submission expected of various groups in the church ([2.1](javascript:void(0))--[10](javascript:void(0))), the theological basis for pious living ([2.11](javascript:void(0))--[15](javascript:void(0))), and a final section bringing the two themes---submission and good works---together ([3.1](javascript:void(0))--[11](javascript:void(0))). The letter concludes with a discussion of travel plans ([3.12](javascript:void(0))--[13](javascript:void(0))), a final exhortation to good works ([3.14](javascript:void(0))), epistolary greetings ([3.15a](javascript:void(0))), and a benediction ([3.15b](javascript:void(0))).

Titus receives a dual task from his mentor, Paul: "putting things in order" ([1.5](javascript:void(0))) by exhorting the faithful in sound teaching ([1.9](javascript:void(0)),[13](javascript:void(0)); [2.1](javascript:void(0))--[2](javascript:void(0)),[8](javascript:void(0))), and refuting the opposition ([2.2](javascript:void(0)),[15](javascript:void(0)); cf. [1.9](javascript:void(0))). The mainstay of sound teaching, as the author defines it, is strict maintenance of a patriarchal church order and the proper submission it demands ([2.5](javascript:void(0)),[9](javascript:void(0)); [3.1](javascript:void(0)); contrast the characterization of the opponents as "insubordinate" or "rebellious" in [1.6](javascript:void(0)),[10](javascript:void(0))). This ethic of the "household code" as applied to the Christian house-church reflects the wider cultural context of Hellenism in the Roman empire and is characteristic of the Pastoral epistles. The second task, the refutation of opponents (depicted as fellow Christians of Jewish background who adhere to the requirements of the law of Moses, the Torah, such as dietary laws), is addressed by the author by sharp invective and ridicule ([1.10](javascript:void(0))--[16](javascript:void(0)); [2.8](javascript:void(0)); [3.9](javascript:void(0))--[11](javascript:void(0))) rather than theological debate, which the author appears to eye largely with suspicion ([1.13](javascript:void(0))--[14](javascript:void(0)); [3.9](javascript:void(0))--[11](javascript:void(0))).

Though short, this letter is theologically packed, requiring readers to pause and reconstruct the underlying gospel narrative and theological concepts, which the author often invokes by terse shorthand. Passages such as [1.1](javascript:void(0))--[3](javascript:void(0)); [2.11](javascript:void(0))--[14](javascript:void(0)); and [3.4](javascript:void(0))--[7](javascript:void(0)) allow for instructive comparison with other tight Pauline formulations (see [Gal 4.1](javascript:void(0))--[11](javascript:void(0)); [Rom 3.21](javascript:void(0))--[26](javascript:void(0)); [2 Tim 1.9](javascript:void(0))--[10](javascript:void(0))), so the theology constructed here can be appreciated both for its distinctiveness and for its continuity with earlier traditions.

*Margaret M. Mitchell*

[**1**](javascript:void(0)) Paul, a servant[^a^](javascript:void(0)) of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, for the sake of the faith of God\'s elect and the knowledge of the truth that is in accordance with godliness, [^2^](javascript:void(0))in the hope of eternal life that God, who never lies, promised before the ages began---[^3^](javascript:void(0))in due time he revealed his word through the proclamation with which I have been entrusted by the command of God our Savior,

[^4^](javascript:void(0))To Titus, my loyal child in the faith we share:

Grace[^b^](javascript:void(0)) and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.

[^5^](javascript:void(0))I left you behind in Crete for this reason, so that you should put in order what remained to be done, and should appoint elders in every town, as I directed you: [^6^](javascript:void(0))someone who is blameless, married only once,[^c^](javascript:void(0)) whose children are believers, not accused of debauchery and not rebellious. [^7^](javascript:void(0))For a bishop,[^d^](javascript:void(0)) as God\'s steward, must be blameless; he must not be arrogant or quick-tempered or addicted to wine or violent or greedy for gain; [^8^](javascript:void(0))but he must be hospitable, a lover of goodness, prudent, upright, devout, and self-controlled. [^9^](javascript:void(0))He must have a firm grasp of the word that is trustworthy in accordance with the teaching, so that he may be able both to preach with sound doctrine and to refute those who contradict it.

[^10^](javascript:void(0))There are also many rebellious people, idle talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision; [^11^](javascript:void(0))they must be silenced, since they are upsetting whole families by teaching for sordid gain what it is not right to teach. [^12^](javascript:void(0))It was one of them, their very own prophet, who said,

"Cretans are always liars, vicious brutes, lazy gluttons."

[^13^](javascript:void(0))That testimony is true. For this reason rebuke them sharply, so that they may become sound in the faith, [^14^](javascript:void(0))not paying attention to Jewish myths or to commandments of those who reject the truth. [^15^](javascript:void(0))To the pure all things are pure, but to the corrupt and unbelieving nothing is pure. Their very minds and consciences are corrupted. [^16^](javascript:void(0))They profess to know God, but they deny him by their actions. They are detestable, disobedient, unfit for any good work.

[**2**](javascript:void(0)) But as for you, teach what is consistent with sound doctrine. [^2^](javascript:void(0))Tell the older men to be temperate, serious, prudent, and sound in faith, in love, and in endurance.

[^3^](javascript:void(0))Likewise, tell the older women to be reverent in behavior, not to be slanderers or slaves to drink; they are to teach what is good, [^4^](javascript:void(0))so that they may encourage the young women to love their husbands, to love their children, [^5^](javascript:void(0))to be self-controlled, chaste, good managers of the household, kind, being submissive to their husbands, so that the word of God may not be discredited.

[^6^](javascript:void(0))Likewise, urge the younger men to be self-controlled. [^7^](javascript:void(0))Show yourself in all respects a model of good works, and in your teaching show integrity, gravity, [^8^](javascript:void(0))and sound speech that cannot be censured; then any opponent will be put to shame, having nothing evil to say of us.

[^9^](javascript:void(0))Tell slaves to be submissive to their masters and to give satisfaction in every respect; they are not to talk back, [^10^](javascript:void(0))not to pilfer, but to show complete and perfect fidelity, so that in everything they may be an ornament to the doctrine of God our Savior.

[^11^](javascript:void(0))For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all,[^a^](javascript:void(0)) [^12^](javascript:void(0))training us to renounce impiety and worldly passions, and in the present age to live lives that are self-controlled, upright, and godly, [^13^](javascript:void(0))while we wait for the blessed hope and the manifestation of the glory of our great God and Savior,[^b^](javascript:void(0)) Jesus Christ. [^14^](javascript:void(0))He it is who gave himself for us that he might redeem us from all iniquity and purify for himself a people of his own who are zealous for good deeds.

[^15^](javascript:void(0))Declare these things; exhort and reprove with all authority.[^c^](javascript:void(0)) Let no one look down on you.

[**3**](javascript:void(0)) Remind them to be subject to rulers and authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work, [^2^](javascript:void(0))to speak evil of no one, to avoid quarreling, to be gentle, and to show every courtesy to everyone. [^3^](javascript:void(0))For we ourselves were once foolish, disobedient, led astray, slaves to various passions and pleasures, passing our days in malice and envy, despicable, hating one another. [^4^](javascript:void(0))But when the goodness and loving kindness of God our Savior appeared, [^5^](javascript:void(0))he saved us, not because of any works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water[^d^](javascript:void(0)) of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit. [^6^](javascript:void(0))This Spirit he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior, [^7^](javascript:void(0))so that, having been justified by his grace, we might become heirs according to the hope of eternal life. [^8^](javascript:void(0))The saying is sure.

I desire that you insist on these things, so that those who have come to believe in God may be careful to devote themselves to good works; these things are excellent and profitable to everyone. [^9^](javascript:void(0))But avoid stupid controversies, genealogies, dissensions, and quarrels about the law, for they are unprofitable and worthless. [^10^](javascript:void(0))After a first and second admonition, have nothing more to do with anyone who causes divisions, [^11^](javascript:void(0))since you know that such a person is perverted and sinful, being self-condemned.

[^12^](javascript:void(0))When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, do your best to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have decided to spend the winter there. [^13^](javascript:void(0))Make every effort to send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way, and see that they lack nothing. [^14^](javascript:void(0))And let people learn to devote themselves to good works in order to meet urgent needs, so that they may not be unproductive.

[^15^](javascript:void(0))All who are with me send greetings to you. Greet those who love us in the faith.

Grace be with all of you.[^a^](javascript:void(0))

**[1.1](javascript:void(0))--[4](javascript:void(0)): Epistolary prescript,** sender, addressee, and salutation with theological expansion reminiscent of Rom 1.2--6 (cf. 1 Cor 2.7; Col 1.26; 2 Tim 1.10). **[2](javascript:void(0)):** *God, who never lies*, cf. v. 12. *Before the ages began*, see 2 Tim 1.9; cf. Jn 1.2--3. **[3](javascript:void(0)):** *God our Savior*, also 2.10; 3.4; 1 Tim 1.1; 2.3; 4.10. **[4](javascript:void(0)):** *Christ Jesus our Savior*, also 2.13; 3.6; 2 Tim 1.10.

**[1.5](javascript:void(0))--[16](javascript:void(0)): Titus\'s commission in Crete.** **[5](javascript:void(0))--[7](javascript:void(0)):** *Elders ... bishop*, apparently regarded as synonymous or at least overlapping categories (cf. 1 Tim 3.1--7; 5.17--20). **[6](javascript:void(0)):** *Rebellious*, lit., "insubordinate" (also 1.10). **[7](javascript:void(0)):** *Steward*, manager of the household (cf. 1 Cor 4.1--2). **[9](javascript:void(0)):** *Sound doctrine*, the reliable tradition the Pastorals pass on; see 1 Tim 4.6n. **[10](javascript:void(0)):** *Those of the circumcision*, Jewish Christians who teach adherence to Torah, the law of Moses (see Gal 2.12), including dietary laws (see v. 15). **[11](javascript:void(0)):** *Upsetting whole families*, lit., "households," the basic unit of civic and church life. **[12](javascript:void(0)):** Invective against opponents supported by a hexameter from the Cretan poet Epimenides (ca. 600 bce). **[13](javascript:void(0)):** *Sound in the faith*, having a "healthy" faith (also 2.2; see 1 Tim 4.6n.). **[14](javascript:void(0)):** *Jewish myths*, probably speculations on biblical texts like Genesis; see 3.9; 1 Tim 1.4; 4.7. **[15](javascript:void(0)):** Cf. Rom 14.14. **[16](javascript:void(0)):** *Good work*, see 2.7,14; 3.1,8,14 (also 3.8n.).

**[2.1](javascript:void(0))--[10](javascript:void(0)): The proclamation of sound teaching in submission.** A catalogue of virtues reflecting and inscribing the hierarchical order of the Greco-Roman household (v. 2, older men; vv. 3--5, women, older and younger; vv. 6--8, younger men; vv. 9--10, slaves). **[2](javascript:void(0)):** *Faith ... love ... endurance*, a variation on Paul\'s usual triad of faith, love, and hope (1 Cor 13.13; 1 Thess 1.3; 5.8; cf. 1 Tim 1.5). **[5](javascript:void(0)):** *Being submissive*, the author seeks to rein in the insubordinate (1.6,10) by calling for obedience to superiors (also 2.9; 3.1) and adherence to the model of Titus (v. 7).

**[2.11](javascript:void(0))--[15](javascript:void(0)): The theological basis for present pious living.** **[11](javascript:void(0)):** *The grace of God has appeared* (lit., "been manifested"), in the life, death, and resurrection of Christ (cf. 3.4). **[13](javascript:void(0)):** *The manifestation* (lit., "epiphany"), a reference to the Second Coming, as elsewhere in the Pastorals (1 Tim 6.14; 2 Tim 1.10; 4.1,8). *Our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ*, if translated this way (see note *b*), is one of the few places in the New Testament where Christ may be referred to as God (Jn 1.18; 20.28; Rom 9.5). **[14](javascript:void(0)):** *Who gave himself*, Gal 1.4; 2.20; Eph 5.2; 1 Tim 2.6. *Redeem us*, buy back from slavery (Rom 3.24; 1 Cor 1.30; 6.20; 7.23; Eph 1.7; Col 1.14; cf. Mk 10.45). *A people of his own*, appropriation of the biblical promise to Israel (Deut 7.6--8; Ex 9.5--16); cf. 1 Pet 2.9.

**[3.1](javascript:void(0))--[11](javascript:void(0)): Submission and good works are the marks of the saved.** **[1](javascript:void(0)):** *Subject to rulers and authorities*, advice for Christians to accommodate to the larger social order (cf. Rom 13.1--7; 1 Tim 2.1--3). **[4](javascript:void(0))--[7](javascript:void(0)):** A tight creedal formulation, perhaps from an early hymn. **[5](javascript:void(0)):** *The water of rebirth and renewal*, baptism, as both promise of resurrection (Rom 6.3--5) and power for present transformation (Rom 12.2). **[8](javascript:void(0)):** *The saying is sure*, a frequent formula in the Pastorals (1 Tim 1.15; 3.1; 4.9; 2 Tim 2.11). *Good works*, as distinguished from "works of righteousness" in v. 5 (the works of the law); see 1.16n. **[9](javascript:void(0))--[11](javascript:void(0)):** Condemnatory attitude toward the opponents (cf. 1 Tim 6.3--5; 2 Tim 2.14--18); cf. the gentler disposition of 1 Tim 2.4; 2 Tim 2.24--26. **[9](javascript:void(0)):** *Genealogies*, linked with "myths" (see 1.4n.) in 1 Tim 1.4.

**[3.12](javascript:void(0))--[13](javascript:void(0)): Travel plans.** **[12](javascript:void(0)):** *Artemas*, otherwise unknown. *Tychicus*, one of Paul\'s companions (Acts 20.4; Eph 6.21--22; Col 4.7; 2 Tim 4.12). *Nicopolis*, probably in western Greece. **[13](javascript:void(0)):** *Zenas the lawyer*, named only here. *Apollos*, an early Christian leader named in 1 Cor 1.12; 16.12; Acts 18.24. *See that they lack nothing*, providing hospitality for itinerant missionaries, as in Rom 16.2; 3 Jn 6. **[14](javascript:void(0)):** *People*, Gk "our people."

**[3.14](javascript:void(0)): Concluding exhortation to good works.**  

**[3.15a](javascript:void(0)): Epistolary greetings.**  

**[3.15b](javascript:void(0)): Concluding benediction.**

[^d^](javascript:void(0)) Or *an overseer*

[^b^](javascript:void(0)) Or *of the great God and our Savior*

#### 2 Timothy (D) c. 90--100 CE

The Second Letter of Paul to Timothy

**NAME, AUTHORSHIP, AND BACKGROUND**

The second letter addressed to Paul\'s "beloved child" Timothy, despite similarities in address and diction, has a more personal tone than the first. (On the authorship and date of this letter, see p. [1725](javascript:void(0)).) Less concerned with church order and roles, here Paul is portrayed as in prison, awaiting trial and expecting death ([2.9](javascript:void(0)); [4.6](javascript:void(0))--[8](javascript:void(0)), [16](javascript:void(0))). In testamentary fashion the apostle hands on to his spiritual heir, Timothy, the wisdom accumulated through a life of mission, ministry, and, above all, suffering for the gospel. The letter is set within a carefully scripted historical scenario marked by Paul\'s imminent death and Timothy\'s bereavement, at a time of distortions to the apostle\'s "sound teaching" ([1.13](javascript:void(0)); see [4.3](javascript:void(0))).

Timothy is named as co-sender of six Pauline letters ([2 Cor 1.1](javascript:void(0)); [Phil 1.1](javascript:void(0)); [Col 1.1](javascript:void(0)); [1 Thess 1.1](javascript:void(0)); [2 Thess 1.1](javascript:void(0)); [Philem 1](javascript:void(0))). They present Timothy as one of his most loyal co-workers, who acted as a trusted delegate to churches ([1 Thess 3.2](javascript:void(0))--[6](javascript:void(0)); [1 Cor 4.17](javascript:void(0)); [16.10](javascript:void(0)); [Phil 2.19](javascript:void(0))--[22](javascript:void(0))). According to Acts 16, Timothy\'s mother was Jewish and his father Greek. That later account imagines that Paul had him circumcised in the face of anticipated Jewish hostility (an event not corroborated in Paul\'s epistles). This letter sketches Timothy\'s life in broad strokes, from his early immersion in the scriptures ([2 Tim 3.15](javascript:void(0))) and matrilineal Christian pedigree ([1.5](javascript:void(0))), to his authorization for ministry by the laying on of Paul\'s hands ([1.6](javascript:void(0))), and his present ecclesiastical challenges. Most prominent in the letter, however, is the detailed and moving portrait of Paul, though ignominiously cast in prison for the gospel in Rome ([1.8](javascript:void(0)),[16](javascript:void(0))--[17](javascript:void(0)); [2.9](javascript:void(0))), forsaken even by close friends ([1.15](javascript:void(0)); [4.10](javascript:void(0)),[16](javascript:void(0))), nonetheless empowered by his Lord not only to endure suffering and death but to celebrate it as the fitting culmination to his life of apostolic ministry and service ([4.6](javascript:void(0))--[8](javascript:void(0)),[17](javascript:void(0))--[18](javascript:void(0))).

**STRUCTURE AND INTERPRETATION**

The theme of 2 Timothy is announced in [1.8](javascript:void(0))**:** Timothy and all who follow him should not be ashamed of the gospel or its representative, Paul, but should stand in fidelity to them, even to the point of suffering. Second Timothy follows a regular epistolary structure with an opening prescript ([1.1](javascript:void(0))--[2](javascript:void(0))), thanksgiving ([1.3](javascript:void(0))--[7](javascript:void(0))), body ([1.8](javascript:void(0))--[4.18](javascript:void(0))), greetings and closing ([4.19](javascript:void(0))--[22](javascript:void(0))). Timothy is urged to contemplate the positive example of Paul ([1.8](javascript:void(0))--[14](javascript:void(0))) and the negative one afforded by those who deserted Paul in time of need ([1.15](javascript:void(0))--[18](javascript:void(0))).

The essential principle of the argument is appeal to example (Paul as one who suffered for the gospel: [1.12](javascript:void(0)); [2.9](javascript:void(0))--[10](javascript:void(0)); [3.11](javascript:void(0)); [4.6](javascript:void(0))--[7](javascript:void(0)), [16](javascript:void(0))--[18](javascript:void(0))), and call for imitation, by Timothy ([2.3](javascript:void(0)); [4.5](javascript:void(0))), and by all readers through him (see especially [2.11](javascript:void(0))--[12](javascript:void(0))). Further, the exhortation to Timothy to be strong and teach others correctly ([2.1](javascript:void(0))--[13](javascript:void(0))) is contrasted with false teachers who must be contended with ([2.14](javascript:void(0))--[26](javascript:void(0))), for, as expected at the end-time, signs of their appearance are already here ([3.1](javascript:void(0))--[9](javascript:void(0))). But Timothy is to follow in Paul\'s footsteps ([3.10](javascript:void(0))--[4.5](javascript:void(0))). These exhortations culminate in the depiction of the dying apostle\'s reflections on his life and its imminent conclusion ([4.6](javascript:void(0))--[8](javascript:void(0)); cf. [Phil 1.12](javascript:void(0))--[26](javascript:void(0))). The letter ends on a hopeful note as the imprisoned Paul exults in divine deliverance (both past and future) and issues spirited directives for the ministry, including a future visit from Timothy ([4.9](javascript:void(0)),[21](javascript:void(0))).

*Margaret M. Mitchell*

[**1**](javascript:void(0)) Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, for the sake of the promise of life that is in Christ Jesus,

[^2^](javascript:void(0))To Timothy, my beloved child:

Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.

[^3^](javascript:void(0))I am grateful to God---whom I worship with a clear conscience, as my ancestors did---when I remember you constantly in my prayers night and day. [^4^](javascript:void(0))Recalling your tears, I long to see you so that I may be filled with joy. [^5^](javascript:void(0))I am reminded of your sincere faith, a faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and now, I am sure, lives in you. [^6^](javascript:void(0))For this reason I remind you to rekindle the gift of God that is within you through the laying on of my hands; [^7^](javascript:void(0))for God did not give us a spirit of cowardice, but rather a spirit of power and of love and of self-discipline.

[^8^](javascript:void(0))Do not be ashamed, then, of the testimony about our Lord or of me his prisoner, but join with me in suffering for the gospel, relying on the power of God, [^9^](javascript:void(0))who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works but according to his own purpose and grace. This grace was given to us in Christ Jesus before the ages began, [^10^](javascript:void(0))but it has now been revealed through the appearing of our Savior Christ Jesus, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel. [^11^](javascript:void(0))For this gospel I was appointed a herald and an apostle and a teacher,[^a^](javascript:void(0)) [^12^](javascript:void(0))and for this reason I suffer as I do. But I am not ashamed, for I know the one in whom I have put my trust, and I am sure that he is able to guard until that day what I have entrusted to him.[^b^](javascript:void(0)) [^13^](javascript:void(0))Hold to the standard of sound teaching that you have heard from me, in the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus. [^14^](javascript:void(0))Guard the good treasure entrusted to you, with the help of the Holy Spirit living in us.

[^15^](javascript:void(0))You are aware that all who are in Asia have turned away from me, including Phygelus and Hermogenes. [^16^](javascript:void(0))May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chain; [^17^](javascript:void(0))when he arrived in Rome, he eagerly[^c^](javascript:void(0)) searched for me and found me [^18^](javascript:void(0))---may the Lord grant that he will find mercy from the Lord on that day! And you know very well how much service he rendered in Ephesus.

[**2**](javascript:void(0)) You then, my child, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus; [^2^](javascript:void(0))and what you have heard from me through many witnesses entrust to faithful people who will be able to teach others as well. [^3^](javascript:void(0))Share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus. [^4^](javascript:void(0))No one serving in the army gets entangled in everyday affairs; the soldier\'s aim is to please the enlisting officer. [^5^](javascript:void(0))And in the case of an athlete, no one is crowned without competing according to the rules. [^6^](javascript:void(0))It is the farmer who does the work who ought to have the first share of the crops. [^7^](javascript:void(0))Think over what I say, for the Lord will give you understanding in all things.

[^8^](javascript:void(0))Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, a descendant of David---that is my gospel, [^9^](javascript:void(0))for which I suffer hardship, even to the point of being chained like a criminal. But the word of God is not chained. [^10^](javascript:void(0))Therefore I endure everything for the sake of the elect, so that they may also obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory. [^11^](javascript:void(0))The saying is sure:

If we have died with him, we will also live with him;

[^12^](javascript:void(0))if we endure, we will also reign with him;

if we deny him, he will also deny us;

[^13^](javascript:void(0))if we are faithless, he remains faithful---

for he cannot deny himself.

[^14^](javascript:void(0))Remind them of this, and warn them before God[^a^](javascript:void(0)) that they are to avoid wrangling over words, which does no good but only ruins those who are listening. [^15^](javascript:void(0))Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved by him, a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly explaining the word of truth. [^16^](javascript:void(0))Avoid profane chatter, for it will lead people into more and more impiety, [^17^](javascript:void(0))and their talk will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus, [^18^](javascript:void(0))who have swerved from the truth by claiming that the resurrection has already taken place. They are upsetting the faith of some. [^19^](javascript:void(0))But God\'s firm foundation stands, bearing this inscription: "The Lord knows those who are his," and, "Let everyone who calls on the name of the Lord turn away from wickedness."

[^20^](javascript:void(0))In a large house there are utensils not only of gold and silver but also of wood and clay, some for special use, some for ordinary. [^21^](javascript:void(0))All who cleanse themselves of the things I have mentioned[^b^](javascript:void(0)) will become special utensils, dedicated and useful to the owner of the house, ready for every good work. [^22^](javascript:void(0))Shun youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, along with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart. [^23^](javascript:void(0))Have nothing to do with stupid and senseless controversies; you know that they breed quarrels. [^24^](javascript:void(0))And the Lord\'s servant[^c^](javascript:void(0)) must not be quarrelsome but kindly to everyone, an apt teacher, patient, [^25^](javascript:void(0))correcting opponents with gentleness. God may perhaps grant that they will repent and come to know the truth, [^26^](javascript:void(0))and that they may escape from the snare of the devil, having been held captive by him to do his will.[^d^](javascript:void(0))

[**3**](javascript:void(0)) You must understand this, that in the last days distressing times will come. [^2^](javascript:void(0))For people will be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boasters, arrogant, abusive, disobedient to their parents, ungrateful, unholy, [^3^](javascript:void(0))inhuman, implacable, slanderers, profligates, brutes, haters of good, [^4^](javascript:void(0))treacherous, reckless, swollen with conceit, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God, [^5^](javascript:void(0))holding to the outward form of godliness but denying its power. Avoid them! [^6^](javascript:void(0))For among them are those who make their way into households and captivate silly women, overwhelmed by their sins and swayed by all kinds of desires, [^7^](javascript:void(0))who are always being instructed and can never arrive at a knowledge of the truth. [^8^](javascript:void(0))As Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these people, of corrupt mind and counterfeit faith, also oppose the truth. [^9^](javascript:void(0))But they will not make much progress, because, as in the case of those two men,[^a^](javascript:void(0)) their folly will become plain to everyone.

[^10^](javascript:void(0))Now you have observed my teaching, my conduct, my aim in life, my faith, my patience, my love, my steadfastness, [^11^](javascript:void(0))my persecutions, and my suffering the things that happened to me in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. What persecutions I endured! Yet the Lord rescued me from all of them. [^12^](javascript:void(0))Indeed, all who want to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted. [^13^](javascript:void(0))But wicked people and impostors will go from bad to worse, deceiving others and being deceived. [^14^](javascript:void(0))But as for you, continue in what you have learned and firmly believed, knowing from whom you learned it, [^15^](javascript:void(0))and how from childhood you have known the sacred writings that are able to instruct you for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus. [^16^](javascript:void(0))All scripture is inspired by God and is[^b^](javascript:void(0)) useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness, [^17^](javascript:void(0))so that everyone who belongs to God may be proficient, equipped for every good work.

[**4**](javascript:void(0)) In the presence of God and of Christ Jesus, who is to judge the living and the dead, and in view of his appearing and his kingdom, I solemnly urge you: [^2^](javascript:void(0))proclaim the message; be persistent whether the time is favorable or unfavorable; convince, rebuke, and encourage, with the utmost patience in teaching. [^3^](javascript:void(0))For the time is coming when people will not put up with sound doctrine, but having itching ears, they will accumulate for themselves teachers to suit their own desires, [^4^](javascript:void(0))and will turn away from listening to the truth and wander away to myths. [^5^](javascript:void(0))As for you, always be sober, endure suffering, do the work of an evangelist, carry out your ministry fully.

[^6^](javascript:void(0))As for me, I am already being poured out as a libation, and the time of my departure has come. [^7^](javascript:void(0))I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith. [^8^](javascript:void(0))From now on there is reserved for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give me on that day, and not only to me but also to all who have longed for his appearing.

[^9^](javascript:void(0))Do your best to come to me soon, [^10^](javascript:void(0))for Demas, in love with this present world, has deserted me and gone to Thessalonica; Crescens has gone to Galatia,[^c^](javascript:void(0)) Titus to Dalmatia. [^11^](javascript:void(0))Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful in my ministry. [^12^](javascript:void(0))I have sent Tychicus to Ephesus. [^13^](javascript:void(0))When you come, bring the cloak that I left with Carpus at Troas, also the books, and above all the parchments. [^14^](javascript:void(0))Alexander the coppersmith did me great harm; the Lord will pay him back for his deeds. [^15^](javascript:void(0))You also must beware of him, for he strongly opposed our message.

[^16^](javascript:void(0))At my first defense no one came to my support, but all deserted me. May it not be counted against them! [^17^](javascript:void(0))But the Lord stood by me and gave me strength, so that through me the message might be fully proclaimed and all the Gentiles might hear it. So I was rescued from the lion\'s mouth. [^18^](javascript:void(0))The Lord will rescue me from every evil attack and save me for his heavenly kingdom. To him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.

[^19^](javascript:void(0))Greet Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus. [^20^](javascript:void(0))Erastus remained in Corinth; Trophimus I left ill in Miletus. [^21^](javascript:void(0))Do your best to come before winter. Eubulus sends greetings to you, as do Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the brothers and sisters.[^a^](javascript:void(0))

[^22^](javascript:void(0))The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you.[^b^](javascript:void(0))
